text_fidelity_a:
Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle I've had this bike a few months now. It is quiet (but not silent, there is a noise from the drive belt) but it is very smooth and responsive.

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

I will update the review if any issues with the bike itself come up. I love the bike, how smooth it runs, and the huge range of resistances available. It seems well-designed and like it will hold up. However, there are some big annoyances that will cost you extra $$$ to overcome.
text_fidelity_b: Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle

text_fidelity_a:
Cathe Friedrich's Supersets & Push Pull DVD (Body Blast series) On this DVD, master instructor Cathe Friedrich offers two workouts from her Body Blast series: Supersets, a strength workout in which exercises are performed in rounds, and Push Pull, a strength workout focused on opposing muscle groups. Both workouts are very good, but what really makes this DVD so valuable is the wide variety of customization options as described below.

Supersets is a 53 minute workout. In each round, Cathe does separate exercises to work the legs, back, chest, shoulders/biceps/triceps, and core. After a brief (4-minute) warm-up, there are a total of two rounds, each broken down into two series (A and B). Cathe encourages participants to lift as heavy as possible, and she incorporates use of a barbell, dumbbells, a stability ball, and unweighted exercises as well. Many exercises are non-traditional in nature, as they include "low end" pluses as well as plyometric moves such as jump squats. The workout makes nice use of the stability ball, particularly for the core work, and Cathe finishes with 5.5 minutes of floor stretches.

Push Pull is a 45-minute, full-body weight training routine which works opposing muscle groups. In some cases, the muscle group is worked with only one exercise, whereas other muscles are targeted with several different exercises. Equipment used for this workout includes a tall step, a stability ball, a barbell, and several sets of dumbbells. The workout begins with a 3-minute warm-up which consists of some light cardio plus stretches using the tall step. Cathe then jumps right in on the legs, performing squats with the barbell, deadlifts, lunges (placing one heel on a smaller barbell to increase the work to the quads), and tall box presses. Moving on to the upper body, Cathe does chest press and rows, then ball work, includnig chest flyes and a "Y" move. Additional upper body work includes a shoulder press off the step, a one-arm row, a front raise while seated on the ball, a rear delt raise lying on the ball, bicep work with one leg on the ball for balance, and tricep dips/kickbacks. Cathe also incorporates the ball for floor leg work such as outer thigh lifts and inner thigh squeezes. There is also additional back work, abs work, and calf raises. Cathe concludes with a short (4.5 minutes) stretch that includes some nice shoulder stretches.

As mentioned above, the best thing about this DVD is the wide variety of custom options. The menus for both Supersets and Push Pull include options for playing the entire workout, viewing the chapter selections, and mixing and matching chapters. In addition, each workout offers "Quick Select Premixes" which provide both shorter and longer workout options. For Supersets, there are 14 premixes ranging in length from 28-109 minutes (these include extra cycles, upper/lower body only, etc.), and for Push Pull, there are 7 premixes ranging from 18-77 minutes which also included upper/lower body only options. Finally, there is a "Workout Blender" option which allows you to create your own custom workout by selecting chapters from either Supersets or Push Pull.

If you are familiar with Cathe, you know that she often incorporates upbeat, recognizable music (selections here include "Goldeneye," "Unbreak My Heart," "Walking in Memphis," and "Breakfast at Tiffany's"). Both workouts are solid, intermediate-level routines which will definitely help you to target virtually every body part from head-to-toe; my overall rating is 4 1/2 starts, and I would definitely recommend this DVD to others.
text_fidelity_b: Cathe Friedrich's Supersets & Push Pull DVD (Body Blast series)

text_fidelity_a:
Marcy Stack Home Gym with Pulley, Arm, and Leg Developer Multifunctional Workout Station for Weightlifting and Bodybuilding You can do a lot with this machine, but it can be a little fiddly to set up. It took so long, I regretted not convincing my roommate we could just do [[ASIN:B004GTLFNW You Are Your Own Gym: The Bible of Bodyweight Exercises]] or [[ASIN:B004XIZN5M Convict Conditioning: How to Bust Free of All Weakness-Using the Lost Secrets of Supreme Survival Strength]] instead. But staying with it was worth it. It's a nice home gym.

First potential issue. Pay attention to when it says tighten and when it says not to. When you put on the central pole (step 2 or 3) you don't tighten it. If you do, step 4 will be impossible. Step 4 may look impossible anyway, because the rear poles will be too low. You have to pull the middle pole forward with one hand, push the rear poles back with another hand, line up the top bar with a third hand, and set up the screws with a fourth. Yeah, it's a good idea to have two people for this stage. And yes, there is a stage where a pully looks like it's just hanging down connected to pretty much nothing. Go with that for the moment. Also, don't make anything too tight.

They give you exactly the number of screws, nuts, and washers you need and not a single screw more. Don't lose one.

You will need a pair of adjustable wrenches. They are not included.

The lateral bar is on what for me seems like too long a chain (even my roommate at 5' tall found it too long) so I would suggest shortening it with the simple expedient of connecting to a lower link. You can always let it back out if you need. You're going to move that bar around from the top to the bottom. There is only one bar provided for both. You will need to use the same carabiner for the bar and for the ankle cuff. I may pick up a spare for convenience sake, but it isn't strictly needed.

There is a child safety lock provided, which I thought was a nice idea.

In use, it provides me enough flexibility I'm happy with it. It provides a chart of how to do each exercise and what each exercise works. I love the lateral pull downs (a good exercise to work up to chin-ups) and that machine always has a line at the gym. No long line for a machine in my living room.

It is small enough I was able to sequester it to a discrete corner of the living room, which is important for an apartment dweller, and it looks fine there. It is large enough to work out on comfortably, but here I'll give the caveat, it's being used by two relatively small women. I don't know if a fairly tall man will find the unit large enough. It might be fine; I just don't know and would be concerned.

There are a lot of options, but most involve using the same thing in different ways (pulling the lat bar behind you, standing and facing the lat bar, puling the lat bar to your chest, etc, etc) so I'll just describe what moves in what way.

You have an overhead lat bar. You can pull it down.
You have two grips. You can insert a pin and move them forward. You can remove the pin for butterfly presses.
You have a leg bar that you can move up.
You have a ring at the bottom that can be connected to an included ankle cuff or the lat bar. You can pull it away from the bottom front center of the machine.

Within that, you have a lot of options, and you will be able to hit every muscle group.
text_fidelity_b: Marcy Stack Home Gym with Pulley, Arm, and Leg Developer Multifunctional Workout Station for Weightlifting and Bodybuilding

text_fidelity_a:
Toogh 2-3-4 Person Camping Tent 60 Seconds Set Up Tent Waterproof Pop Up Hexagon Outdoor Sports Tent Camping Sun Shelters, Instant Cabin Tent, Advanced Venting Design, Provide Top Rainfly It took me a little bit to figure out how it all works, but once you get it I'm pretty confident that the "60 second" claim is accurate. It's insanely fast to pop up this tent! I thought that would mean it is insanely hard to put it away as some other pop-up-style tents seem to be. But surprisingly it wasn't hard to all to put away once you understand how it unbuckles. At first I think I almost broke it trying to figure it out- You don't force it to bend, you have to pull up on the joint to unlock it otherwise it might snap and break. The instructions weren't clear on that, but once you get it, honestly, it's pretty fast and simple. I'm impressed.
It's also pretty roomy inside. We all know when a tent says "3-4 Person" they mean really more like 2, but more can squeeze like sardines if they are skinny. Well, I had 3 kids stay in here, age 4 to 11, and they did NOT feel cramped (see picture- the sides weren't even spread out all the way since it was indoors and a couch was in the way). I climbed in to hang out with them for a bit, and I can honestly say one roughly 190lb dad and 3 kids fit inside and it didn't seem too crazy in there. It's also pretty tall for a small tent- my kids can stand inside easily and not hit the ceiling.
Would easily recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Toogh 2-3-4 Person Camping Tent 60 Seconds Set Up Tent Waterproof Pop Up Hexagon Outdoor Sports Tent Camping Sun Shelters, Instant Cabin Tent, Advanced Venting Design, Provide Top Rainfly

ROCHAN Slingshot with Solid Wooden Handle Professional Hunting Sling Shot with 1 Rubber Bands Wrist Rocket Slingshots for Adults … This is a strong and durable slingshot, and definitely not for children. It comes with 4 sets of rubber bands, a container of 56 steel balls (supposed to be 100), 2 Allen wrenches, flashlight bracket, and magnetic keyring. What it did NOT include that was supposed to be included was the other 44 steel balls and the 100 mud balls were not included at all. There were also no instructions whatsoever.

Even without instructions this slingshot for the most part was easy to put together since I have other slingshots I have had to assemble. The rubber bands and wrist support (which is a great feature!) assembled fine, and each side of the handle has a lovely dragon image. The flashlight connector was another matter. I was able to get it affixed to the slingshot, but 2 of the components on the connector itself do not fit together well, so it cannot be fully tightened. So I decided not to use the flashlight connector at all.

Another thing I did not like was that one of the sights of the slingshot had a lot of excess metal that I had to file down. I used a metal file to do this, but had to file quite a bit out of the inside of that one site, and the outside of both left and right sights also needed some filing as well.

My final thoughts: This is a powerful slingshot and not a toy. It’s a really nice looking slingshot and can be accurate if you know how to shoot a slingshot. But due to the lack of instructions, missing pieces, the need to file the sights, and the flashlight connecter not being able to tighten properly, I cannot in good conscience give this item more than 3 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids. I purchased this to use on my bicycle that I use for commuting. I leave early in the morning while it is still dark. The route I take is pretty well lit with street lights so I use the lights mostly for visibility and not to light the road in front of me.

The mounts are pretty simple to use. I attached the front to the handlebar and the back to the basket I have on the rear rack. The front light has 3 steady settings at 3 levels of brightness and one flashing mode. I am not sure how useful the level of brightness would be in absolute darkness as far as seeing the path in front of you because I have not used it in that scenario, but it seems pretty bright to me. I keep it on flashing mode for visibility. It is conveniently re-chargeable via USB cord and it seems to last adequately between charges.

I gave this product a 3 star rating because the back light does not work the way I need it to. The first time I used it, I thought I turned it on but when I got to my destination it was off so I figured I forgot to turn it on. The second time I used it on the return trip, I made absolutely sure it was on when I started and when I got to the destination it was off again. I took the light off my bike and turned it on and dropped it onto a hard surface from a distance of less than 3 inches and it shut off. Since this is battery operated and not rechargeable, I'm guessing the batteries get jolted from going over a bump on the road and shuts off on its own. It lights up again without any issues if you press the on button again, but that is not feasible or safe to reach behind you and fix it if you are riding on a road with vehicular traffic all around you. It is also very inconvenient to pull over to the side every time it shuts off to turn it back on again. Since the light set was fairly inexpensive, I just purchased a different separate backlight from the local box store to replace it.

I will not go through the time and inconvenience of returning the item or exchanging it because it simply is not worth it. I hope the seller doesn't try to contact me to "fix" the problem because they will be wasting their time.
text_fidelity_b: BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids.

Coleman Pack Away LED Mini Lantern (Colors May Vary) I purchased the [[ASIN:B0018S4XIS Rayovac Sportsman LED Lantern (SE3DLNA)]] and this Coleman mini lantern. Both are bright but this pack away mini is great for when I need a little less light or want to carry a lantern that performs almost as well as the Rayovac but in a lot smaller package. For instance, this would be great to carry when walking outside in the dark because it's very light (about 8 ounces) and bright and makes a person visible enough to be seen.

What I like about this lantern is:
- It takes 4 AA batteries instead of the "highly in demand" D batteries that most flashlights use.
- The mini lantern fits in the palm of my hand when I collapse the LED portion into the unit.
- Mine came with a mini carabiner that I could hook onto the handle for easy carrying on a pant belt loop or backpack.
- The bottom battery compartment screws out by hand by turning the plastic grip several times until the cap came off.
- There are three modes of high, low, and strobe. The low mode does not look low to me and seems very similar to high but it's supposed to save battery life. Just pressing and releasing the top black button changes the mode.
- When the unit is collapsed, the light cannot accidentally be turned on which is a great feature.
- The unit is relatively light compared to full-sized lanterns.
- The package claims the LED lasts a lifetime and never has to be changed.

I purchased this at WallMart for $19.99 plus tax ($21.39) which is $1.60 less than Amazon's current price of $22.99.

This mini lantern suits me for small jobs and lights up my bathroom or kitchen with enough light to see without being blinding. In summary, there isn't anything I don't like about this lantern.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Pack Away LED Mini Lantern (Colors May Vary)

Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30 What a great reel for big, powerful fish! If you target fish that measure in the hundreds of pounds, and you want the best tool for the job, this is your reel. In my case, it's the reel I use when we go deep for big halibut here in Alaska. This reel holds plenty of line to get to those shelves 400 feet down where the barndoors lie, with plenty of line left over to allow for long runs that those big fish make. If you hang up and break off, losing several hundred feet of line (it happens), you don't have to hang it up because the reel holds enough line to let you keep fishing.

I like the high-speed retrieve for pulling up from the deep when you need to check your bait or try something else. When you latch into a fish, though, a quick push of the button on the hub of the handle engages the more powerful lower gears, so you can really torque into the fish.

That new handle design is nice, too. It comfortably fits my hand, has a nice rubbery, no-slip texture, and helps spread the stress across the meaty part of my hand so long battles are just a little bit easier.

The open design of the "X" series frame (with no crossbars across the front of the spool) is helpful when there's a backlash to deal with (yeah, it still happens once in a while). These reels aren't cheap, but they're the best you can buy. Solid, reliable, and made in USA. No regrets here!

Let me know if you don't anything in my review helpful.

A super tiny Philipps screwdriver is needed to get into either battery compartment.

Then I tested the batteries that came with the unit in a bike light I have and the batteries worked. The headlamp is junk and that is disappointing. I am unsure if that is the case for others or if the batteries were included by mistake for the lantern or not. Also, I do not know what the "flash eyes" comment means on the Amazon site. My Amazon Review Criteria:
5 Star: I got what I expected from the product and it was/worked better than expected. If you are considering a purchase, buy it. Would buy it again, I highly recommend.

4 Star: I got what I expected from the product and that is all. It just works. Still recommend the Item, probably hard to find a better product than this. Would buy again, I highly recommend.

3 Star: I got what I expected from the product most of the time. Has a few problems but it can be overlooked. Might buy the product again, but will look for other alternatives as well. I recommend the product, there might be better alternatives.

2 Star: I barely got what I expected from the product. Has many problems, product is bad. Would not buy again. I do not recommend buying this product unless there are no other alternatives.

1 Star: I never got what I expected from the product. Would not buy the product again, requested a refund or returned the product. (This is very rare for me.) I do not recommend buying this product whatsoever.

The new redesigned camelbak valve on these is a huge improvement over the older ones, they seem to be more resistant to getting moldy in the first place.. and if they do it is quick and easy to disassemble for cleaning! Great job camelbak!

My only qualm with these bottles is that the plastic is very soft and gets marred/scratched very easily. This was kind of the case with the older camelbak bottles also but it seems even worse on these newer ones. It doesn't affect the function of the bottles so its not a huge issue but just kind of annoying that these look old and beat up after one or two rides whereas I have some other (non-camelbak) bottles that are several years old and still look practically new. That said, those other bottles use harder plastic which is more rigid and more difficult to squeeze, making them harder to drink from, and the ease of squeezing out a large amount of liquid is what makes the camelbak bottles so great, so its a tradeoff I'm willing to make..

I've noticed some reviewers complaining about them not fitting well in bottle cages but I've never had issues on any of my bikes, I use arundel cages on most of them but I have also have some specialized and lezyne cages.

Wake Bike Stem Riser Bike Fork Stem Extender Bicycle Handlebar Raiser Head Up Adapter Suitable for Mountain Bike, Road Bike, MTB, BMX, Fixie (Aluminium Alloy, Adjustable) This WAKE stem riser comes with enough spacer-rings to put your existing handlebar riser at the right height and allow the stem cap and long stem bolt to fully engage. There was a little difficulty in keeping the alignment of the now top and bottom sections of this taller riser assembly, but I found getting the top on first and clamping it in position so the gaps in top and bottom line up vertically is easier than putting the tall riser on first and then aligning and tightening the top section with the handlebars to it. It can be done either way, but it took a lot of fussing, tightening and loosening and twisting. Getting that long bolt in to press the stem cap down to hold everything in position is complicated that the fork bearing will keep everything loose without the correct alignment, so you have to keep that as a goal because nothing can have a final position without that important fork bearing being seated. Then, all you need to do is clamp it all together on the bike. This is a 2 part operation: the long bolt and stem cap forces the assembled units together and down, then clamping the top and bottom riser sections together and to the bike for a solid steering connection. I think this better than the older-style threaded stem which depends on that single bolt to hold everything in place.
-Compressing in several dimensions makes it more secure.-
The test ride, once I was satisfied that everything had been aligned and tightened, was different from how the bike had been only an hour ago. My hands, arms and shoulders were at a more natural angle and riding was much easier. This riser extension is only 2.7 inches, but coupled with the top riser and raised handlebars the difference is more than 8 inches overall. A nice, comfortable ride!
There are youtube videos showing this operation in detail. //// It's important to do it properly! ////
text_fidelity_b: Wake Bike Stem Riser Bike Fork Stem Extender Bicycle Handlebar Raiser Head Up Adapter Suitable for Mountain Bike, Road Bike, MTB, BMX, Fixie (Aluminium Alloy, Adjustable)

text_fidelity_a:
Biscuits & Gravy | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings I was really surprised at how well they hit the exact flavor and consistency that I love from biscuits and gravy with this meal! This was my first mountain house dehydrated meal that I have ever eaten, and I learned a lot from testing it out. I actually picked up a few flavors in the last couple weeks just to taste them and know which ones I would actually like to bring backpacking or keep in my emergency supply kit.

What I learned from this is that I need to make sure that my water is seriously boiling hot and not just boiled five minutes ago. I also need to measure extremely carefully and definitely not short it on water. And also I need to not worry about the meal getting soggy, and instead taste a bite, and close the packet again and let it soak in some more if that is not fully rehydrated.

Overall, this was a perfect introduction to how fresh and delicious food like this can taste. We actually had some garden zucchini to eat on the side, and so having the biscuits and gravy, a fried egg, and some garden zucchini, all able to be cooked up on the camping stove, was amazing! It felt like a full, amazing meal, and even if I didn't have the egg or zucchini available, I would've been very happy to eat this.

In addition, there are some types of wheat that really bother me, and I wanted to find out if the wheat used in this product gave me that specific allergic reaction that I get to so many, even high quality, foods. I was absolutely delighted to find out that I did not experience any of the itching, swollen eyes, or other sensations that I occasionally get from eating wheat from certain brands. I am now feeling more confident to test out different flavors from this brand and definitely will include this specific flavor in my camping and emergency supply box. The portion size was enough to feed both myself, and my four and six-year-old kids, with accessory foods on the side to fill out the meal.
text_fidelity_b: Biscuits & Gravy | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings

text_fidelity_a:
Hewolf Camping Sleeping Bag Waterproof - Compact Indoor Outdoor Sleeping Bags 4 Season Great for Adults Kids Youth Teen can be Zipped Together (Blue, Single 32-50F/0-10℃(1.8kg)-Right Zip) This bag arrives snugly packed in a compression bag that is small enough to easily pack into or strapped onto a backpack, either internal or external frame. Unpacking the bag from this sack was a bit of a challenge as the compression straps are sewn onto the sack and move just enough to get the bag out.

I was pleased with the way the bag looked, the outer shell is a slick navy and medium blue poly that does seem to be at least water resistant because when I poured a glass of water on it the water did bead up and did not soak into the bag. The interior is a grey, lighter weight and slightly brushed poly that feels much more pleasant than some sleeping bag interiors that i have used - not as slick. The zippers, and there are two, are a heavy nylon and have a grosgrain draft barrier on the inside. The long zipper on the side has metal tabs on both the inside and outside. There is an addition slide at the lower end of this zipper for further adjustments. A separate, similar zipper is across the bottom. The way the bottom is configured it appears as though the bag cannot be fully opened. Additionally there is a quarter inch or so gap between the two zippers at the corner so a very small amount of cold air might infiltrate.

There is a permanently attached hood on this bag. If not needed for warmth it can be quite wide and used as just a place to rest a pillow. In cold weather the hood can be drawn in quite snuggly by use of a drawstring. On the inside of the bag there is a soft sewn in tube to keep drafts from entering around the neck. There is also a clever little pocket on the inside near the neck just perfect for tucking a phone.

As for size - I am a woman, 5'6" and average weight and found the bag quite comfortable. It is tapered but roomier than a true mummy. I don't think this would be a good choice for anyone 6 feet tall or over, or for anyone more than a few pounds overweight.

I had no problem operating the drawstring, zippers, etc. Putting the bag back into the stuff sack was an average amount of trouble for returning a bag into a sack.

There is information printed on the stuff sack but it is in Chinese so I can only guess about what it says. The bit that I take to be a temperature comfort range indicates this as a warm weather bag 40 to 60 degrees Fahrenheit, although 0 Celsius is mentioned (32 Fahrenheit). If sleeping without a shelter and with minimal ground cover the 50 to 60 would be correct, with appropriate ground cover (pad, ground sheet etc) it could go lower, and with a tent down to just above freezing should be fine.

This is an inexpensive bag but surprisingly well made considering the modest price and filled with some features usually reserved for more expensive bags. Besides the ones mentioned there are tabs on the bottom so the bag can easily be hung up to dry or air out. Also this bag comes in right or left zips, and two bags, (one of each configuration) can be zipped together - making this an excellent choice for couples. text_fidelity_a:
GoSports Fitness Core Hub Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration for Full Body Workouts - Blue or Red So far so good with this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration. I’d seen a similar product in commercials and wondered if it would actually work for planking - or was it a gimmick. When I had the chance to grab this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration I took it, hoping it would add to my workout options. For various reasons I prefer not to plank directly on the ground, so would this be of help? The answer for me is, yes. As I continue to adjust to using it.

It arrives with the platform itself, pump, and instructions. One assembles the platform simply by pumping air into the ball on the bottom. My wife and I found this was a two person job - the long needle easily went in, however, it also easily pumped out until I had her hold it in place. At that point the ball quickly and easily pumped to full size. Pulling the needle out the air stayed in and there was no leaking - with nothing to plug it - and a week later holds the air perfectly. They included a second pin for the end of the pump - great if the first breaks or is lost, but we’ve found the first one wouldn’t even come off after we secured it.

There is a plastic covering on the phone “t” so don’t forget to remove it. It easily comes off and the foam under holds the phone in place just fine - though I haven’t used the phone or any app for working out at this point - I do have it there for stop watch.

I’ve put some pounds on since surgery so I wondered how it would hold the weight and so far it’s fine. I don’t feel any weakness or bowing or any issue in holding me up. As a shorter guy with shorter arm length I do find that positioning my arms in a spot to make placement comfortable is not exact. In fact, I end up testing my forearms a bit to hold on. And it’s taking time to find the best spot for being comfortable on the platform. Plus having the platform lay right in oder to balance correctly. Still working it, but also, still getting a solid workout. In fact I come away each time feeling the burn and it’s been a solid way to plank. It can be used in either the kneeling or full out, extended leg position and while I’ve only done it fully extended, I can see the benefits to both options.

So, does the movement and/or height add to the benefit of planking? I have to think it does. I like being up off the floor and having a nice, comfortable surface under my arms. As for the movement, it does work the fuller core area and I feel the burn in more than just one spot. I’ve only done this for a week, twice a day most days, and I’m doing better at time at the end of that week. I will maybe add in the app-games, but right now that is not my personal interest - but I can see how it could add to the fun (I’m not a gamer).

Any cons? So far it’s a little too early to know overall - will the board last, how does the app work...
I did notice there is a ’sound’ when laying on the board under the forearms. It seems like it might indicate the surface material could separate from the hard plastic base.

I do have an issue in reaching the handles under the platform - for grip I hold the side of the platform. It might be nice to have a grip along the side one can hold onto other than these two handles.

As long as the ball holds up - and I so far do not see why it won’t hold up - it can be a good, solid exercise platform. But that foam on the top needs to also remain. If that comes off, it will affect the platform itself. So far it’s fine, but again, what does that sound mean - other times I’ve heard it things have separated.

In the end I so far believe this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration is a great find and will help me with my workouts and to improve physically. I’m enjoying the experience and I’m enjoying the possibilities of how to continue planking in a fun manner. So yes, I do like this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration and happy to give it a 5 star rating.
text_fidelity_b: GoSports Fitness Core Hub Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration for Full Body Workouts - Blue or Red

First of all, don't disregard people's reviews where they state that the colors are off or completely different than advertised. I purchased the Grey blanket which shows in the picture as a mix of black and/or dark grey, white, and light grey. The blankets I received are a mix of black, light grey, white, and muted purple (see picture). The good news is, I like the color and don't mind the purple. The purple isn't super dark but it isn't lavender either so I am fine with it.

I am returning one blanket for a replacement for a different reason though. I know these blankets are hand woven and expect some pulling etc. but one already has a rather large pull leading to a two inch string (apparently with two ends tied together) and a section about three inches wide with a hole in the middle. I just don't trust that it won't come unraveled or get bigger once I start to use it so I will be asking for a replacement (hopefully I will receive the same "wrong color" that I did this time).

The blankets are a little thinner than the ones at the yoga studio but not significantly so to cause a problem for me.

I do like the look and feel of them so I hope that I can come back and add a star to this review after a few weeks of use.
text_fidelity_b: YogaAccessories Traditional Mexican Yoga Blanket

Elastic Weight Training. This is an observation, not a criticism. In my opinion, the bands don't offer enough resistance to really be used for building muscle size. They might be better considered as used for toning. What I've done is combine all five bands together, which do provide a fair amount of resistance (I've also had to tie on a 6th loose band to get the resistance I want). Fortunately, the 'D' ring that the bands attach to on the handle is large enough to add several bands. This kit does appear to be of high quality, and I have no issue with that, and for certain exercises I'm sure one or two bands work fine. I got them to hang on the door, and do the "band pull-up" move where I have one knee and one foot on the floor, and pull them toward me. My suggestion is to hang them close to the hinge side of the door so you don't put extra pressure on the doorknob side, lest it burst open (trust me on that one).

EDIT: I have to update this, because I kind of messed up. I failed to notice these come in a variety of tension sets. I ordered the "105 pound" set, which means if you add up the tension in all 5 bands, it comes to 105 pounds, which I didn't find to be enough. I should have ordered the "150 pound" set. In fact, I did go ahead and exchange the smaller set for the larger one with no problem. Just be careful to order the correct set of tensions!

text_fidelity_a: Daiwa Crossfire Front Drag Spinning Fishing Reel ( I was in the market for a 4000 series spinning reel and after reading about several different reels, this Daiwa Crossfire Front Drag Spinning Reel caught my attention.  I have seen this reel offered for sale in the marketplace, as a combo, by a dealer who would put them on a more expensive rod for sale.  I didn't know much about the quality of this specific reel, but it felt pretty smooth and the evident quality of the rod would sell the combo.  I didn't sucker for the $100 combo, but I did remember the reel, as Crossfire kind of stuck in my head.  When I got a deal for $25.95 on one with free shipping, I took it and am satisfied with the quality of Diawa's spin reel.  I have learned that the acceptable quality of the newer reels offered, hold up fairly well and better than those in past years at lower prices.  I have several reels, in my library of used equipment, that are inferior in quality to about anything out there that I would consider paying for.  Here on the Gulf of Mexico coast where I fish, the environment on the shore, bays and on the boat causes some problems for reels.  Corrosion can occur when you forget to rinse your reel off after each time out, in hot weather when you come home spent and you just sit your rodnreels down in the front of the garage and then you grab and open a beer, only to forget them until it is too late.  It's surely the beer combined with the heat that causes this.  This reel has a anodized spool and holds up as well as any I've owned.  My other reels have all experience my neglect and for the price this reel performs well and seems good with the neglect.  I do now try to rinse them each time though, but braid holds moisture more than mono and I used braid on this reel.  So, I hope it continues to perform.  If not, I will return to this review and adjust the comments and Stars to reflect what happens.  I like it though and at this time will purchase more in the future. I am sure I will respect and take better care of this Reel, and the Diawa Sweepfire rod it is on, than in the past!  I recommend this combination of rod and reel and will purchase Diawa fishing equipment in the future.
text_fidelity_b: Daiwa Crossfire Front Drag Spinning Fishing Reel (

Thule Aspect DSLR Large Shoulder Bag, Black I have a really nice 12 year old Olympus camera that has been all over the world with me and has documented my best memories & experiences. The different carrying cases have never lived up to the expectations or sometimes harsh environments my beloved camera has.

This Thule bag is surprisingly well made and much bigger than my best case. (See the photo for side by side comparison) This bag holds my camera and a portable tripod with some finagling of the included padded pieces. Those pieces are designed with Velcro to fit and attach in whatever shape or spot you need - which means you aren't limited to using only items that fit in pre-made pockets.

The zippered lid pocket has a perfect pouch for batteries, USB cords and other small odds and ends. Inside the bag is a separate pocket for a tablet. Once I put my camera and tripod in, my 10" Fire will only fit if I take the case off of it first, so that's not great. There are two elastic pockets on the outside and a flat front zippered pocket on the front with a snap for your keys. Conceivably, you could hit the trail with just this bag carrying your camera stuff, a bottle of water, your id & keys and maybe a light, small snack. I have had this out at the barn & a horse show for photos of the horses and it works fine, but it will take some time to get used to the bulk of this bag for trekking through a jungle or climbing ruins in Central America or Asia.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Aspect DSLR Large Shoulder Bag, Black

text_fidelity_a:
AmazonCommercial Rotomolded Coolers, 45 Quart Towable, White 20 quart Capacity:

I was hoping for mobile cooler that would be good for holding a decent amount of food or drinks. The cooler is very durable and robust. It is sturdy enough for someone to stand on without even deflecting the lid. The seal between the top of the cooler and the main compartment is tight. The hinges are molded out of the rotomolded plastic. It also has rubber feet. This reminds me of the type of cooler that would be used to transport organs by a hospital - very high quality with no doubt that it will keep the products inside cool for a long period of time.

Unfortunately, it did not satisfy my needs. I didn't realize how small the interior capacity would be. The exterior dimensions of the cooler are 12 inch deep x 19-1/2 inches and the inside dimensions are 8 inches x 14--1/2. That means the cooler is 4-5 inches thick at some locations, which is obvious by the heavy weight of the cooler. With nothing inside, the cooler weighs around 17 pounds, which doesn't sound like much, but it is relatively heavy for what you would expect for a cooler of this size and capacity.

The other thing that I don't love is the big 'amazon commercial' yellow sticker on the front that sticks out like a sore thumb. Of course, they need to market their product, but they could have added branding in a more subtle way.

45 quart Capacity:
The 45 quart capacity has all the same features and attributes as the 20 quart, but just a little larger and heavier. I think this one is versatile and functional.
Exterior Dimensions: 27 inches x 15-1/4 inch
Interior Dimensions: 21-1/2 x 11 in
Empty Weight: 26-1/2 lb

I got these doubleshot pedals for my commuter bike. Really nice to have the option to use either flat shoes or cleated shoes on the same pedals. The pedals are big enough that the flat side is very stable and flipping to the side you want is easy. The cleated side is easy enough to click in and out. It feels a little different from the eggbeater pedals, but I got used to that quickly. I use the same shoes/cleats that I use with the eggbeater pedals with no problems. A new set of Crank Brothers cleats is included with the pedals for people that are new to Crank Brothers.

I'm using the cheapest 1-series version of these pedals. The 2-series has more durable bearings, which frequent users will probably want. The 3-series has the improved bearings as well as adjustable studs on the flat side of the pedal. Use a small hex wrench to raise or lower the stud height. This is a nice feature if you want to fine tune studs' grip to your shoes (or lower them entirely so they don't chew up your shoes).
